verified_reason: Li & Sheykhlouvand 2025: double-blind RCT, creatine 0.1 g/kg/d vs placebo (plus beta-alanine, citrulline, combined and no-training control arms; n=8 each), 28 d, basketball players. The stated training is short sprint interval training 3x/wk; outcomes are jump, sprint, change of direction, Wingate and cardiorespiratory tests. The abstract names no RT and no eligible outcome, but does not rule RT out in an athlete sample, and no open full text exists (not in PMC). The sister trial from the same lab (SP8-0349) had no RT in its full text, so expect E03/E05. Only the full text can decide

E03: resolved from the open full text (PMC13564169). Duan 2026: creatine monohydrate, ethyl ester or HCl vs placebo (n=10 each), 28 d, collegiate soccer players. Training was soccer practice 5 d/wk plus repeated sprint training 3 d/wk; no resistance or gym training is described anywhere in the methods. Outcomes are jump, 20-m sprint, L-run, Wingate and VO2max; body mass is given at baseline only (E05 also applies)

E06: preprint of SP1-1141 (Papadimitriou 2026, Muscles; same authors and abstract), which was excluded E06. The published full text (PMC13692481) confirms a narrative/hypothesis review: eligible evidence included case reports, narrative reviews, in vitro and animal studies, with no restriction to trials, and it states there are no clinical trials of creatine in Crohn's disease. Not an SR/MA of trials; deduped to the published version

Thesis (Worthington 2016, Aberystwyth): intervention studies of long-term creatine and of 12 wk 'high-intensity exercise' with creatine in adult women; bone density, body composition, muscle strength. The Europe PMC abstract is truncated and the repository is not reachable from this session; exercise type (RT or interval training), comparator, age and duration of the creatine arms are not stated. A web-search summary of the repository abstract says creatine did not augment the exercise effect but did raise strength. Only the thesis can decide

Thesis (Guppy 2013/2014, Aberystwyth): 12 wk circuit exercise vs non-exercising controls, with creatine reported to have no effect on body composition or bone (DXA); a later study adds creatine to interval training (that part would be E03). Whether the circuit programme is resistance-based, whether creatine was compared with placebo inside the exercise arm, and participant age are not stated in the truncated abstract (extra detail from a web-search summary of the repository record only). Only the thesis can decide

E07: thesis (Touba 2008, Liverpool John Moores). Every study in the thesis is an acute fatigue-and-recovery design around a single heavy resistance-exercise challenge in women (isometric force, rate of force development, recovery to 48 h); the creatine study tests recovery after that challenge. No RT programme in any study, so the supplementation length cannot make it eligible (E03 is an alternative code). Based on the Europe PMC abstract plus a web-search summary of the repository record; thesis PDF not read

Thesis (Pittas 2006, Nottingham): includes a study of prolonged creatine with resistance training; DXA lean tissue, dynamometry strength, muscle gene expression. Abstract truncated before that study: comparator (placebo or only creatine formulations, which would be E04), duration, n and age are not stated. The 2024 paper from this thesis (Pittas et al., Transl Exerc Biomed) appears to cover only the loading/maintenance studies, so the RT study may exist only in the thesis. Only the thesis can decide

Seyf 2014 (journal not identified, vol 6 pp 175-189, probably Iranian): RT and creatine on strength and flexed-arm girth in female students. No abstract in Semantic Scholar, no DOI, nothing in Europe PMC. Title suggests a creatine + RT trial; design, comparator, duration and language unknown (E12 possible). Only the full text can decide

Johnson 2006: undergraduate research report (Univ. Wisconsin-Eau Claire), creatine monohydrate with an RT programme and 1RM bench press in college-age men. No abstract (Semantic Scholar summary line only); comparator, randomisation and duration unknown. Not peer reviewed; expect E15 or E04 once the report is read, but that cannot be decided from the record

E07: Kuwamori 2008 (Research Journal of Budo). J-STAGE is not reachable, but the abstract text returned by web search describes 14 collegiate judo athletes (7 men, 7 women) who took a glucose placebo for 6 days and were re-tested, then took creatine: a short-term single-group placebo-then-creatine loading design with isokinetic thigh strength, repeated 10-s cycling and body composition. No RT programme and no parallel comparator (E04 also applies). Supports the E13 call on its meeting abstract SS1-0181. Based on search-result text, not the article page

E06: Miny 2017 (Science & Sports 32:61-72). The ORBi abstract, as returned by web search, uses the journal's general-review headings (Objectives / News / Prospects and projects / Conclusion), 'takes stock of current knowledge' and gives practical dosing advice; no databases, eligibility criteria or count of studies. Narrative review by the SP7-0013 precedent. Soccer is already covered by the included SRs SP8-0212 and SP1-1131. Based on search-result text; the repository page itself is not reachable

E14: preprint; whey protein + creatine HCl + glutamine vs no supplement in 11 university athletes during 4 months of strength training; multi-ingredient vs nothing, creatine effect not isolable; allocation not described as random
E06: preprint; narrative review of vegetarian diets and athletic performance; creatine mentioned only as a dietary nutrient

E03: preprint (Erdogmus 2023). 15 physically active men, Wingate-based HIIT 3 d/wk for 6 wk with or without creatine 10 g on training days; no placebo. The abstract defines the whole training programme as HIIT, so RT is positively absent; leg strength is an outcome but there is no RT programme in either arm. Same call as SP1-0296 and SP8-0105. Its published version SS1-0479 should get the same code

E01: fish feeding trial (red drum), dietary creatine and guanidinoacetic acid

E03: date palm pollen and DOMS after eccentric exercise in female athletes; no creatine (no abstract; Semantic Scholar summary line and title)

Confirmed on the title and the convention (multi-ingredient product vs plain placebo). I could not retrieve the abstract or full text (not in Semantic Scholar, Crossref, PubMed or Europe PMC; publisher site not reachable), so the ingredient list and placebo composition are NOT independently verified; the screener's details (n=40, 4 wk, kidney-function parameters) are taken on trust

E07: thesis (Mihic, McMaster): short-term creatine vs placebo, whole-body protein turnover in 27 recreationally active adults; no RT programme, no eligible outcome

E03: confirmed from the open full text (PMC12157024). Yamaguchi 2025: creatine vs cellulose placebo for 33 d in 40 healthy adults (mean 26 y) who had NOT done regular training for more than six months, then one bout of eccentric elbow-flexor exercise; recovery of MVC, stiffness, soreness. No RT programme. Funded by Taisho Pharmaceutical

E07: single-blind crossover of placebo, taurine, creatine and taurine + creatine in 12 sports students; time to exhaustion and repeated sprints in heat; acute test sessions, no RT programme, no eligible outcome (E05 also applies). Supplementation length is not in the abstract and the full text is not open

E14: McGregor & Sewell 2007: carbohydrate + protein + creatine vs carbohydrate alone for 5-10 wk in 12 swimmers and triathletes; creatine cannot be separated from protein, and no RT is indicated in endurance athletes. No abstract (Semantic Scholar summary line only)

E12: Spanish-language systematic review (Retos 2018, English abstract only) of strength training plus supplementation in vegetarians; 3 studies, all creatine. Citation chasing: Burke 2003 = SP1-0147 (included), Burke 2008 = SP1-0271 (included), Shomrat 2000 (PMID 10958375) is NOT in records.csv but is a 1-week creatine study with Wingate tests and no RT (would be E07), so nothing eligible is missing. The English-language SR on vegetarians SP8-0224 is already included

E03: confirmed from the open text (PMC3500735). Conference abstract (JISSN 2012) of Kresta 2014 = SP1-0477 (E03): 28 d creatine and/or beta-alanine vs placebo in 32 recreationally active women; the abstract states the study did not include a training protocol

Include. Preprint (Preprints.org, Singh 2025): 12 male students randomised to creatine, glycogen loading or control, all doing the same 6-wk structured weight-training programme; strength, hypertrophy, adiposity. Meets the PICOS on the abstract: the protocol accepts a no-creatine comparator under the same RT, it is randomised, and 6 wk meets both duration minimums. Flags: preprint=yes, about 4 per arm, no placebo or blinding (F-BLIND), dose not stated, method of the hypertrophy measure unknown (may be girths, not eligible), check for a published version. High risk of bias; no conclusion may rest on it

Include as SR/MA mapping. Preprint (Preprints.org) meta-analysis of creatine alone or with RT in older adults with sarcopenia: PRISMA 2020, three named databases, 14 studies, lean mass and leg-press outcomes. Creatine-specific and its criteria admit creatine vs placebo trials with RT, so it passes the SR/MA rule (clinical/older population does not count). Flags: preprint=yes, check for a published version, mapping and citation chasing only

Include as SR/MA mapping, with a caveat. Conference abstract (Br J Surg 2026) of a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of creatine in knee osteoarthritis / total knee arthroplasty: 4 OA RCTs plus older-adult creatine + RT trials, with results stated. Creatine-specific and admits creatine + RT vs placebo RCTs, so it passes the SR/MA rule, and E13 does not apply because results are given. But it is abstract only: no reference list, databases not named, so it cannot feed citation chasing or be appraised with AMSTAR 2 unless a full paper is found. Chase the full publication; if none, code E13/E10 at full text

Preprint (Preprints.org, Delbiondo 2026): RCT, 51 perimenopausal women (46.2 +/- 4.6 y) randomised to creatine (20 g/d for 5 d, then 4.5 g/d), placebo or non-training control; creatine and placebo arms did 6 wk of high-intensity RT; DXA lean soft tissue, pQCT muscle area, ultrasound CSA, upper and lower body strength. Mean age is inside 18-50 and no range is given, so it goes to full text for the range; perimenopause is not a disease; 6 wk meets the hypertrophy minimum. Same trial as SP1-1142 (Baker 2026, Eur J Appl Physiol: n=51, 46 +/- 5 y, same three arms, same lab, NCT07027800), so SP1-1142 should be recoded E08 with this as the primary report. Flags: preprint=yes, check for a published version, F-COI (senior author advises creatine companies), and the abstract's conclusion overstates a creatine vs placebo lean-tissue difference of 0.38 kg with p=0.999
